info.name: Portfolio & Orders API
info.description: One request per case, with basic assertions. Use it with the `local` environment against the local docker-compose Postgres: the order requests WRITE orders for user 1, so never point `baseUrl` at an API connected to a shared or remote database. Reset the data with `docker compose down -v`.

item.description: Idempotent order creation: every order carries a required `clientOrderId`.

exec: pm.test('order has an id and an ISO datetime', () => {

request.description: The client chooses a required id for each order. If the request is repeated with the same id, no second order is created. The id is generated in the pre-request script of this request.

exec: pm.test('returns the order that already exists', () => pm.expect(order.id).to.eql(Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('idempotentOrderId'))));
pm.test('the order is unchanged', () => { pm.expect(order.status).to.eql('FILLED'); pm.expect(order.size).to.eql(1); });

request.description: A repeated clientOrderId answers 200 with the original order instead of creating another one (a new order answers 201).

item.name: Orders - cancellation
item.description: Cancellation of NEW orders. Run after `Orders - accepted`: it uses the order ids stored by that folder.

exec: pm.test('order is the one created by the LIMIT BUY request', () => pm.expect(order.id).to.eql(Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('limitOrderId'))));

request.description: Only NEW orders can be cancelled. The funds it committed are released automatically. Depends on `LIMIT BUY by quantity`, which stores the order id in `limitOrderId`.

exec: pm.test('succeeds again and the order stays CANCELLED', () => pm.expect(order.status).to.eql('CANCELLED'));

request.description: Repeating a cancellation is safe: it answers 200 with the same order and changes nothing, so clients can retry after a network failure.
